subject: Private VPC deployment — control plane & data plane networking review

Subject: Request: Private VPC deployment review (control plane/data plane)

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. Acme Health is planning a Private deployment for several regulated workloads (PHI in scope) and we need a short architecture review focused on control plane placement, data plane connectivity, and network segmentation. High-level asks:

- Confirm whether the control plane can remain in Redwood-managed SaaS with private peering to our VPC, or whether a customer-managed control plane is required for our compliance boundary.
- Review the recommended data-plane topology for inference traffic: private endpoints, NAT/Egress patterns, and KV cache synchronization across on-prem and cloud.
- Discuss KMS/HSM options for key material and audit log retention for SOC2 / HITRUST evidence.

I attached a rough topology diagram and the compliance checklist we are using. Can we do a 30–45 minute technical review next week? Our security lead (Karl) will join.

Appreciate it — Nadia
Nadia Ortiz
Director, IT Architecture
Acme Health

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC deployment review (control plane/data plane)

Nadia — thanks for the clear asks and the sketch. We can run a focused review. Quick answers up-front, to narrow the agenda: 

1) Control plane placement: For PHI workloads we typically recommend a customer-managed control plane (Private deployment) when customers require full network isolation and no control-plane metadata leaves the VPC. That said, we have a hybrid pattern where Redwood hosts a slim control plane (management plane only) with private peering + strict egress rules for audit telemetry — acceptable to some auditors. We'll surface the trade-offs.

2) Data plane topology: Preferred pattern is private load balancers (no public IPs), SNAT at egress gateways or NAT instances in a dedicated egress subnet, and explicit VPC endpoints for model inference. KV cache replication uses a TLS-mutual-auth tunnel between data-plane nodes and is locked down to specific subnets.

3) KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS keys (Cloud KMS/HSM) with envelope encryption. For on-prem HSMs we can integrate via an HSM gateway or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow.

Proposed time: Wednesday 2026-08-12 11:00–11:45 PT. I'll bring Karthik (infra/network) and Hannah (security/ops). Attached: initial-controlplane-dataflow-v1.pdf (diagram).

If that slot works I'll send an invite plus a short pre-meeting checklist.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek / team —

Interlock Systems will be the network integrator for this engagement. A couple of notes from our side that might affect the diagram:

- We prefer to terminate customer BGP on a virtual router in the data-center VPC and peer to the Redwood private endpoint via an AWS Transit Gateway (or equivalent). This avoids cross-account peering for each environment.
- For on-prem fallback, we recommend a TLS-based tunnel with healthchecks and a route-preference failover to the cloud data plane.
- We attached our adapter spec (interlock-network-adapter-spec.md) with port/ACL recommendations and expected MTU.

Happy to jump on the call and walk the network bits.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Briggs
Solutions Architect, Interlock Systems

Attachment: interlock-network-adapter-spec.md

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC deployment review (control plane/data plane)

Tom / Nadia / team —

Thanks for the adapter spec. A few items I'd like to confirm ahead of the meeting so we can be prescriptive:

- Control plane telemetry: if the control plane is Redwood-hosted, we will require a one-way egress-only path from the control plane to a telemetry collector you host in the customer VPC (TLS, mTLS optional). If telemetry must remain in-customer, we will recommend the customer-managed control plane option.
- Subnet layout: Plan on three subnets per AZ: control-plane mgmt, data-plane inference, and egress/nat. Ingress will be limited to the inference subnet via SGs and NACLs.
- KV cache replication frequency: default is eventual with async replication; for synchronous cache we require dedicated low-latency connectivity (Direct Connect/MPLS equivalent).
- Audit logs: retention policy and whether they must remain in our control or can be pushed to your long-term archive (S3 with lifecycle policies).

Action items for the call:
- Nadia: confirm if Acme requires the control plane to be inside customer network (yes/no).
- Acme Security: provide the list of approved CAs for mTLS.
- Interlock: confirm TGW design and whether they need a Transit VPC or can use TGW attachments per account.

I'll capture these into SUP-3456 and update the diagram post-call.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
